final_message:
Phase 5 is finished: every required suite passes with zero failures and zero not-implemented, and everything is committed (33 commits on top of the baseline, clean working tree).

## Test results
- **All phases:** phase 1 225/225, phase 2 186/186, phase 3 143/143, phase 5 15/15. `TOTAL: 569/569 pass`.
- **`--modes`:** phase 1 1350/1350, phase 2 1116/1116, phase 3 858/858. `TOTAL: 3324/3324 pass`.
- **HTTP:** conformance over HTTP 569/569; `http suite: 18/18 passed`.
- **Build:** `make build` works from a clean checkout offline; `make test` passes (117 unit tests) and `make lint` (clippy) reports no warnings.

The conformance tables are too small to trigger parallelism on their own, so I also ran the `--modes` matrix with 7-row morsels to force it (3324/3324). Two extra checks are in `bench/`:
- **`difftest.py`** generates random queries and compares every option combination against row mode running the same plan. Over 6,000 queries found no differences.
- **`bigdiff.py`** runs 24 queries on the 1M-row datasets, including a memory-mapped PQCF copy, under five configurations. All agree.

## What I implemented
- **`mode: row`** is the unchanged Phase 4 engine, kept as the single-threaded baseline. Its top-N selection now breaks ties by input order (deterministic) and it gained a merge join.
- **`mode: vectorized`** (also used for `auto`, the default) processes batches of 2,048 rows over typed column vectors. Dictionary-encoded strings stay encoded through filters, grouping, joins and sorting. It covers filtering, aggregation, hash/merge/nested-loop joins, radix sorting and top-N.
- **`threads`** runs scan pipelines in parallel in fixed-size chunks (morsels): output keeps serial row order, aggregation and DISTINCT merge partial results by hash partition, and large non-integer sorts split across threads. The default is the CPU count, capped at 16.
- **`join`**: `hash`, `merge` and `nested_loop` are all supported and show up as the required node names in EXPLAIN; `auto` uses a hash join, building on the smaller estimated side.
- **`optimize`** turns on constant folding, predicate simplification, predicate pushdown and statistics-based join reordering.
- **`native: true`** is accepted but has no effect.

## Main design decisions
- **Errors match row mode exactly.** If a vectorized or parallel run fails with a data error before returning any row, the query is re-run in row mode and that result or error is reported. So `SELECT 10/x … LIMIT 1` behaves the same in every mode.
- **AND/OR errors don't depend on plan shape.** An error in one operand is raised only if the other operand doesn't already decide the result (the spec leaves this case implementation-defined). This keeps `optimize: true` and `false` from disagreeing on whether a query fails.
- **`optimize: false` still prunes columns** (scans read only referenced columns) and still picks index scans for filters directly on a table, because the existing EXPLAIN tests require both under every option combination.

## Measurements (1M-row datasets, ms; the shared host adds up to ±25% noise)

| Query | Phase 4 engine | `mode: row` | vectorized, 1 thread | vectorized, 8 threads |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Filter + COUNT | 86 | 85 | 3 | 1 |
| 1M ⋈ 100k join + GROUP BY | 212 | 277 | 15 | 4 |
| Full sort of 1M rows | 523 | 430 | 39 | 18 |
| 500k-group GROUP BY | 513 | 600 | 44 | 27 |

The README has the full 12-query table, `optimize`/join-algorithm comparisons, and commands to reproduce them.

## Known limitations
- Row mode never uses more than one thread.
- Merge joins, building the hash-join table, and correlated subqueries (which run in the row engine) execute serially.
- With more than one thread, float SUM/AVG can differ in the last bits; the spec allows this and tests compare floats with a tolerance. Integer and decimal sums are exact in every mode.
- Native kernels are never loaded.
- Join reordering applies only to inner and cross joins.
